content:
We need retrosynthesis up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to propose route using templates. We need to find suitable disconnections. Molecule: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which is para-substituted with the cinnamoyl anilide (trans). Could disconnect at sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also disconnect at amide formation (acid chloride + amine). Also disconnect at C=C formation via Wittig or Heck coupling.

Goal: <=3 steps. Perhaps two steps: step1: sulfonylation of aniline (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline bearing the cinnamoyl side chain). Step2: formation of the cinnamoyl amide via coupling of trans-cinnamic acid chloride with aniline (or via amide coupling). But the aniline also has sulfonamide later, so order may be reversed.

We could start from commercially available p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, TsCl) and aniline derivative that already has the cinnamoyl amide attached: N-(3-phenylprop-2-enoyl)aniline? Actually the target has an aniline attached to the amide: C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl ring). The amide is attached to the phenyl ring via carbonyl carbon, and the nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline). So the amide is N-phenyl cinnamamide (cinnamoyl anilide). So we need aniline (aniline) reacting with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give N-phenylcinnamamide. That product then undergoes sulfonylation at the aniline nitrogen? Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the other phenyl (p-tolyl) via nitrogen attached to the phenyl ring (the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring of the sulfonyl group). Actually structure: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3 N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (p-tolyl) and to the sulfonyl group, and the sulfonyl group attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing the cinnamoyl amide). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (as substituent) and the sulfonyl group attaches to the second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is not part of the amide; the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para? actually it's attached to the amide carbonyl). So there are two aniline nitrogens: one is part of sulfonamide (attached to tolyl), the other is part of amide (attached to phenyl). The amide nitrogen also has a free NH (since N attached to phenyl and carbonyl). So we have two aromatic amines.

Thus route: Step1: Synthesize the sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride is commercial). React with the second phenyl ring (which is a phenyl bearing the cinnamoyl amide) to give sulfonamide. So need the phenyl bearing the cinnamoyl amide (call it 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl). That could be made via amide formation between 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) and trans-cinnamoyl chloride. So step2: amide formation. Starting materials: p-aminophenyl (p-aminobenzene) is commercial (aniline). trans-cinnamoyl chloride is commercial? Might be available. Or trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) can be converted to acid chloride via thionyl chloride (extra step). But we have only 3 steps total. Could do amide coupling using EDC/HOBt etc directly from acid and amine (one step). So step2: couple trans-cinnamic acid with p-aminophenyl to give N-(4-aminophenyl)trans-cinnamamide (which still has free NH on phenyl). That's our intermediate (call it I). Step3: sulfonylation of I's free amine (the aniline) with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride to give final product. That is 3 steps total.

Check leaves: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) commercial, trans-cinnamic acid commercial, aniline commercial. All likely buyable. Need to ensure price total < $9999. Likely yes.

Now need to produce JSON route with reactions and template IDs. Need to find appropriate template IDs for sulfonylation (sulfonyl chloride + amine) and amide coupling (acid + amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups broken/formed.

Let's search for amide formation template.
